# crypt_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Encrypt or decrypt files in place with GPG.

## Synopsis

```
crypt_tool [options]
```

## Description

Processes the given file, or every file under the given directory, and writes the
result next to the original. Encryption uses GPG symmetric AES-256. An encrypted file
is named after the MD5 of its original filename plus `.enc` (for example
`document.pdf` becomes `<md5>.enc`), and the original filename is stored inside it.
Decryption reads that stored name back and restores `document.pdf`.

The passphrase is read from the `[UserData.Protection]` section of the configuration,
never from the command line: `general_passphrase` for `-t General`, `locker_passphrase`
for `-t Locker`. The originals are deleted after a successful run unless `-k` is given.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | File, or directory of files, to encrypt or decrypt; must exist. |
| `-t, --passphrase_type <General\|Locker>` | Which configured passphrase to use: `General` (`general_passphrase`) or `Locker` (`locker_passphrase`). Allowed: `General`, `Locker`. |
| `-e, --encrypt` | Encrypt each file to `<md5 of name>.enc` beside it. |
| `-d, --decrypt` | Decrypt each `.enc` file back to its stored original name beside it. |
| `-k, --keep_originals` | Keep the original files instead of deleting them after processing. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Encrypt every file in a directory with the locker passphrase

```bash
crypt_tool -i /path/to/files -e -t Locker
```

### Preview an encryption without changing anything

```bash
crypt_tool -i /path/to/files -e -t Locker -p -v
```

### Decrypt previously encrypted files

```bash
crypt_tool -i /path/to/encrypted/files -d -t Locker
```

### Encrypt files but keep the unencrypted originals

```bash
crypt_tool -i /path/to/files -e -t Locker -k
```

### Encrypt a single file with the general passphrase

```bash
crypt_tool -i /path/to/file.txt -e -t General
```

## Notes

- `-t` is effectively required: without it no passphrase is found and the tool stops.
- Give exactly one of `-e` or `-d`; with neither, nothing is done. `-e` wins if both are given.
- A file whose output already exists is skipped and its original is kept. Files already in the target form (`.enc` or `.menc` when encrypting, anything else when decrypting) are left alone.
- Locker encryption normally uses `locker_passphrase`, but a locker with its own `locker_<name>_passphrase` setting encrypts with that instead, and those files need `backup_tool` to decrypt.
- To encrypt or decrypt while copying to another location, use `backup_tool -r`.
